Larry F. Taylor, Jr. is a trial attorney who represents families in birth injury, medical malpractice, traumatic brain injury, mass torts and serious accident cases nationwide. Known as the RealLyfe Lawyer, he has spent nearly two decades taking on hospitals, corporations and insurance companies on behalf of people whose lives were changed by someone else's negligence, no matter where in the country they call home.

Larry has handled complex medical-negligence, mass tort and catastrophic-injury cases, working with physicians, nurses and life-care planners to prove what went wrong and what it will cost a family over a lifetime.

A closer look at three cases

blocks.title: Birth injury — delayed C-section resulting in hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy
blocks.description: A family came to us after their child was diagnosed with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy following a delayed emergency C-section. We worked with independent OB-GYN and neonatology experts to pin down exactly where the standard of care broke down, then built a life-care plan reflecting decades of specialized medical needs the family will face. The case resolved before trial under a confidentiality agreement.

blocks.title: Medical malpractice — missed diagnosis leading to permanent injury
blocks.description: A client's diagnosis was missed for months despite clear warning signs in the chart, delaying treatment until the condition had progressed significantly. We worked with independent medical experts to show exactly how the standard of care was breached, and took the case in front of a jury rather than accept an inadequate offer.

blocks.title: Mass tort — dangerous drug / defective device claim
blocks.description: As part of a coordinated multidistrict litigation, we represented a client injured by a dangerous drug that reached the market without adequate long-term safety data. Working alongside co-counsel across multiple states, we helped secure a resolution reflecting the full scope of our client's ongoing medical needs.

items.q: Why do some case results show 'Confidential'?
items.a: Many settlements include a confidentiality agreement as a condition of resolution. We honor those agreements while still being transparent that a result was achieved.

items.q: Does a big verdict or settlement mean my case is worth the same?
items.a: No. Every case depends on its own facts — the injuries, liability, available insurance and applicable law. A free case review is the only way to get an honest read on your situation.

items.q: Do you take cases to trial, or only settle?
items.a: We prepare every case as if it will go to trial. Most cases settle, but we're ready to try a case when that's what's best for our client.

blocks.title: Free case review
blocks.text: Call or submit our form 24/7. We listen, ask questions, and tell you honestly whether we can help.

blocks.text: We gather medical records, accident reports and expert opinions to establish liability.

blocks.title: Case building
blocks.text: We file your claim and build the evidence and expert testimony needed to support it.

blocks.title: Negotiation or trial
blocks.text: We negotiate from a position of strength — and we're ready to try your case if the other side won't be fair.

blocks.title: Resolution
blocks.text: You get answers — and if we recover compensation, our fee only comes from that recovery.

items.q: How long does a case take?

items.q: Will I have to go to trial?

items.q: What if I've already talked to the insurance company?
items.a: Tell us what was said as soon as possible — we can often still help, but earlier is better.
